## [#10933: fix: prevent stacked Sheet backdrop flashes in Firefox](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10933)

- **Change:** low complexity, a single-component RAC fix for nested Sheet users: 27 changed source lines in `Sheet.tsx`, plus two test files, using the existing browser-test harness rather than adding infrastructure. Revision: `05d1d6a2f57f931d446f541a8fb4da0a499624ad`.
- **Issue and direction:** [#10924](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10924) reports that an unregistered child initially reuses `--sheet-timeline-0`, causing the parent backdrop to bind to the child in Firefox. All returned issue comments were read. Member reidbarber [confirmed the bug and recommended](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10924#issuecomment-6663457398) "a stable unique timeline name independent of its index." The [new name at Sheet.tsx lines 249-260](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/05d1d6a2f57f931d446f541a8fb4da0a499624ad/packages/react-aria-components/src/Sheet.tsx#L249-L260) exists before registration; descendants, backdrop animations and content declarations now use it. This plausibly addresses the reported collision and follows the agreed direction, by reading only.
- **Compatibility:** no public prop, export, type, event, default, DOM structure, class or data-attribute change was found. Generated inline `view-timeline-name`, `animation-timeline` and root `timeline-scope` values do change from index-based names to ID-based names ([Sheet.tsx lines 168-173](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/05d1d6a2f57f931d446f541a8fb4da0a499624ad/packages/react-aria-components/src/Sheet.tsx#L168-L173), [1117-1123](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/05d1d6a2f57f931d446f541a8fb4da0a499624ad/packages/react-aria-components/src/Sheet.tsx#L1117-L1123)). Consumers hard-coding the old names would be affected; the current main docs describe `swipeAnimation` and `stackAnimation`, not those generated names. Stack order and styling attributes remain index-based. No `needs API review` recommendation on this evidence.
- **Verification gap:** [Sheet.browser.test.tsx lines 65-86](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/05d1d6a2f57f931d446f541a8fb4da0a499624ad/packages/react-aria-components/test/Sheet.browser.test.tsx#L65-L86) use `it.skipIf(!CSS.supports('animation-timeline: view()'))`. [Main's Firefox instance](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/8203ef81549ef9e01391a57b2e244b13cf36daaa/vitest.browser.config.ts#L259-L280) supplies no enabling preference. Therefore green browser CI alone does not establish that Firefox exercised this bug; the author's enabled-Firefox before/after and manual results remain unverified claims. The browser cases do exercise real opening/closing, three-level nesting and rendered backdrop opacity, unlike the supplemental unit assertions about timeline identity. Their two attempts reopen inner sheets while the outer remains open; they do not automate the issue's fresh outer-sheet reopening, which the manual instructions explicitly include.
- **Existing solution / red flags:** `origin/main:packages/react-aria-components/src/Sheet.tsx` still generates names from stack indices at lines 170-172; the fix is not already incorporated. The [issue's CSS workaround](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10924), `.react-aria-SheetBackdrop[data-has-descendants] { animation: none !important; }`, uses the supported descendant-state selector but sacrifices synchronized backdrop animation rather than fixing timeline identity. It is a temporary workaround, not an equivalent replacement for the agreed fix. No added suppression, unsafe cast, accessibility removal or production timing hack was identified. The existing `@ts-ignore` and non-null assertions are unchanged; added `requestAnimationFrame` calls sample test frames, not delay production behavior. No CI workflow, manifest, dependency, lockfile, install script or build-config changes trigger the mandatory security-review flag.
- **Duplicates:** searches covered #10924, Sheet/Firefox, backdrop flashes, timeline behavior and recent mentions of `Sheet.tsx`. No supported competing implementation was found. Closed [#10835](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10835) touches the same component/test filename but adds a `scrollend` exit fallback for a missing observer report, not this backdrop collision. Merged [#10674](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10674) introduced Sheet; its [index-versus-ID discussion](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10674#discussion_r4127917114) is prior design context, not a duplicate. #10924 is the originating issue, not a duplicate to close.
- **Labels (proposed):** add `merge-risk: medium` for changed animation bindings and the enabled-Firefox verification gap; `small review` for the focused low-complexity component fix; `ai-reviewed` for completed read-only triage with limitations recorded; `has workaround` for the supported-selector CSS mitigation; `waiting for maintainer` for the next substantive review. Recommend maintainer-only `ready for review`, because direction, relevant tests and manual instructions are present, CLA is signed and no attributable failing CI check is returned. All proposed labels exist. Remove none; keep existing `RAC`.
- **Maintainer next step:** ready for substantive review on the available read-only evidence. Review timeline identity and the generated-CSS compatibility change, and confirm enabled-Firefox evidence, including closing/reopening the outer sheet. [Returned checks](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10933/checks), including CLA, lint, unit/browser/SSR tests and type comparison, are successful; no author blocker is asserted. Confidence is medium on browser correctness because no code was run and the Firefox capability gate prevents inferring coverage from CI success.
